resources.string: The recovery key unlocks the backup of your encryption keys. With it, a new device can read your earlier encrypted messages. The server cannot read the backup. Keep the key somewhere safe: nobody, not even the server, can recover it for you.
Creates a new backup with a new backup key under the same recovery key, for example if you suspect that the backup key leaked. Needs your password.
You already have a backup. A new recovery key replaces it: the old key stops working, and keys that only the old backup has are lost. If you have the old key, restore your history instead.
Write it down or save it to a file. It is shown only now.
Other apps and keyboards with a clipboard history can read the clipboard. It is cleared after a minute. Writing the key down is safer.
Copied. The clipboard is cleared in a minute.
I have saved my recovery key
The keys of your encrypted chats are backed up from now on.
Enter your recovery key (or its passphrase) to read your earlier encrypted messages on this device.
There is a typo in the recovery key
Will be used as a passphrase
Messages read with keys from the backup are marked “sender not confirmed”: the backup cannot prove who wrote them.
There is a typo in the recovery key.
This is not the recovery key (or passphrase) of your backup.
There is no backup on the server.
The backup on the server does not match its recovery data. It was not used.
The server could not be reached. Try again.
To read your earlier encrypted messages here, verify this device with another of your devices, or restore your history with the recovery key.
Create a recovery key, so you can read your encrypted messages on a new phone too.
